title: CILantro run manifest
description: What `cilantro --json` prints on standard output: one run, said in one object. Everything the run wrote is named here, so a caller never has to rebuild a path from the naming convention.

Schema.description: Which version of this shape the object is. Read it first and refuse a major version you were not written for.

Success.description: Whether the run finished with something to stand behind. The same answer as exit code 0.

Strict.description: Whether the run refused rather than assuming anything about the machine the sample expects.

Protector.description: Which protector the run settled on, by the name a program uses, or "none". Said outright because more than one is recognized and the capability list alone does not tell two of them apart: both name a capability anti-tamper and mean different mechanisms by it.

Protections.description: What the file was found to be protected with, by the tool's own names for them.

Payloads.description: What was hidden inside the file, each with the path it was written to.

RebuiltMethods.description: How many methods that shipped as bytecode for an interpreter are code in the cleaned copy.

RebuiltCheck.description: What running the cleaned copy established about those bodies. `agreed` means it unpacked the same payload the original did.

VerificationDiagnostics.description: Why the cleaned copy was withheld, where it was.

Blockers.description: What stopped the run, each carrying what to declare to get past it where a declaration would.

ContinuedPast.description: How many calls a non-strict run walked past rather than stopping at. Named in full in the blocker report.

MoreToDeclare.description: Whether any stop has a remedy, which is to say whether running again with a fuller declarations file could get further. False with stops still listed means the rest need a change to the tool, and a caller looping on this sample should stop.

Cleaned.description: The readable copy of the assembly, or null where the run had nothing it could stand behind.

Config.description: The constants a protector kept out of the metadata, written beside the assembly because they cannot all be put back into it. Null where the sample kept none there.

Listings.description: The programs behind virtualized methods, as text: two files per method, the operations as read and the same thing as IL.
